editorial:
Imagine being torn between what you love and what your parents want for you. You get to see this struggle first-hand through Saunders, a kid from the Bronx who is absolutely killing it in the Litefeet dance scene. While he is dodging trains and winning dance battles in the subway, his dad is pushing him toward a boring engineering degree. The vibe here is electric and feels like a love letter to New York City. Teyana Taylor brings a great eye for style and movement, making the dance scenes feel alive rather than staged. You will really feel for Saunders as he tries to keep his two worlds from crashing into each other.

The acting feels natural, and the music will have you tapping your feet the whole time. Some parts of the story feel a bit predictable, but the energy keeps you moving. If you love movies about chasing your dreams, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final act, Saunders enters a huge dance competition that his father accidentally finds out about. Instead of getting angry, his dad sees the joy and discipline Saunders puts into his art. Saunders wins the battle with a mind-blowing routine. The movie ends with his father agreeing to let him pursue dance as long as he stays in school. It is a happy ending where both father and son finally understand each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dance movies and stories about family conflict.
